title: The key names the server sends and their scan codes
covers: The key names the DOSBox-X server carries into the guest, and the scan set 1 make code each of them is sent as.

rows.text: In the list's make code table the 0 key is written 0 ).
The make code of 0 ) is 0Bh.
DOSBox-X answers it as KBD_0 of KEYBOARD_AddKey1, which the dispatcher calls when keyb.cb_xlat is set or the scan set is 1.

searched.gave: The DOSBox-X mouse code cites no document for its button numbers.
No maker document names a PC mouse button; the button is a name of the server's own input table.
Not searched: a mouse button is not a part a datasheet numbers.
Not searched: a mouse button is not a part a datasheet numbers.
Ralf Brown's make code table writes [Note2] left mouse as 7Eh, a scan code of the Schneider/Amstrad PC1512 keyboards' mouse, not this button.

rows.text: DOSBox-X gives button 0 to the left button: it sets bit 0 of mouse.buttons and queues MOUSE_LEFT_PRESSED, doing nothing if bit 0 is already set.
When the machine is not a PC-98 and the keyboard AUX port is active, button 0 sets bit 0 of mouse.buttons and sends the state to KEYBOARD_AUX_Event.
Mouse_ButtonPressed reaches button 0 through a case 0 in each of its two switches on button.
